h.strategy: Most obvious hypotheses follow a local story: an option matters more when its substitute is missing. These are usually rated likely and often fail. Instead, base hypotheses on robust statistical regularities. (1) Headroom: helpful edits help less in parents that are already strong, for example parents that already contain the strongest option elsewhere. (2) Harmful edits hurt more in strong parents and look harmless in weak parents, because of floor effects. (3) Saturation: adding a second copy of a strong option gives smaller gains than adding the first. (4) Removing an option costs less when the parent has several similar options. Choose conditions that many parents satisfy, so the effect is detectable. Cover several edited fields and both directions. In each 'why', state the obvious prediction and the reason the opposite should hold.

hyps.why: A 1x1 conv on edge 0 might seem to add diversity next to a 3x3 conv, but parents already holding the strongest op have less headroom for any helpful edit.
One could argue 1x1 complements 3x3, but a strong parallel conv into the output leaves little room for improvement.
Skip paths seem always beneficial, but a second identity-like route to the output is redundant once edge 3 already provides one.
Removing edge 5 seems uniformly bad, but when edge 4 already carries a strong conv into the output, the loss is buffered by the similar option.
Cutting edge 2 starves node 2 less when edge 1 already supplies conv features to it, so the removal costs less.
Pooling on edge 1 is usually harmful, but it becomes harmless when node 2 is disconnected from the output via edge 5 = none.
One might think a strong conv upstream compensates for pooling, but harmful edits hurt more in strong parents, while weak parents sit near the floor.
A strong parallel conv could seem to mask pooling, but strong parents have more accuracy to lose, so the damage is larger.
A conv path to the output might seem to make the direct edge redundant, but conv-heavy strong parents rely on the residual-like edge 3 and lose more from the harmful edit.
A direct conv to the output might seem complementary to the node-1 path, but saturation of strong ops into node 3 shrinks its benefit.
